newsitem.title: MEXICO: Televisa ready to launch DTH TV in Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Televisa ready to launch DTH TV in Mexico.

text.p: Mexican media firm Grupo Televisa SA said on Monday it is only weeks away from launching its direct-to-home (DTH) satellite television service in most of the country.

Sky Entertainment Services, the brandname for the joint venture between Televisa, News Corp Ltd., Brazilian media giant Globo and U.S. cable company TCI, will begin offering its service in Mexico City next week, according to Jorge Alvarez, the head of Sky in Mexico.

"The week after next we expect to offer services in Guadalajara, Monterrey, Aguascalientes, Puebla, Tijuana and Los Cabos. Maybe a month or so later we will offer it nationally," Alvarez said at a news conference.

Sky will charge customers 3,190 pesos for installation of the satellite equipment and a decoder box plus between 200 and 460 pesos per month for different packages of channels. It offers up to 60 channels of digital video and 34 channels of digital audio.
Alvarez said he expects to have signed up between 170,000 and 200,000 customers by the end of 1997. He said the company estimates the potential market right now is about 1.5 million subscribers.

He said Sky has eight satellite transponders ready to go and will have 12 by February or March. They have 15,000 to 20,000 decoder boxes in Mexico right now and plan to import up to 50,000 more boxes.

Sky's main competitor, DIRECTV Latin America, has already been in operation for more than a month here. DIRECTV is a joint venture between Hughes's Galaxy, Mexico's Multivision, Venezuela's Venevision and Brazil's TV Abril.
